text.title: Activation Tactics Worked Example
text.summary: One complete playbook step for a B2B SaaS with three measured drop-offs: a 3-item checklist on the project-creation screen and a 3-send verification email sequence, each with a rollout step and a numeric exit criterion, a deferral branch for the step that already has a live tactic, with a note on each non-obvious value; then the playbook step as it is usually written and what the validator prints.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: Activation is `project_created` within 7 days. The activation-metrics report ranks "project created" (32.6 percent step conversion from `/projects/new`) and "email verified" (73 percent) as the top drop-offs; "workspace named" converts at 94 percent and already carries a live tooltip experiment. Users who stall on project creation are inside the product; users who never verify have left. No use-case key is captured at signup.

example.title: checklist on /projects/new plus verification sequence
example.note: Both tactics name a step from `dropoffs[]` and carry that step's conversion as `step_conversion_baseline`, which is the number the exit criterion is later measured against (r-tactic-targets-named-dropoff-step). The checklist has three items: `workspace_named` is checked by its tracked event with no navigation, `first_project` is the single `activation_event: true` item and is required, and `invite` is optional; nothing on the list can be ticked by hand (r-checklist-single-activation-item). The email sequence targets "email verified" because a user who never verified has left the product, and every CTA is the authenticated verification link, not the home page; `expected_time_minutes: 1` is stated in each body (r-email-one-cta-direct-link). Days 1 and 3 carry `not_activated` evaluated at send time, Day 0 is the only unconditional send, three sends stay inside the 7-day window, and the Day 7 email from the template was dropped because verification either happens in the first days or not at all (r-email-sequence-suppressed-on-activation). No guide was placed on `/workspace/setup` because that step converts at 94 percent and already has a live tactic (r-in-app-guide-at-dropoff-only). No segmentation because no use-case key exists at signup (r-segmented-onboarding-keyed-at-signup). Each rollout step states metric, baseline and the lift that keeps the tactic: 0.326 + 0.03 for the checklist, 0.73 + 0.05 for the emails (r-exit-criterion-states-metric-and-threshold). The `defer_live_tactic` branch is what kept "workspace named" out of this period's tactics (r-one-tactic-per-step-at-a-time).

example.title: the same product's tactics as usually written
example.note: What the validator prints: the checklist has 6 items, above the maximum of 5, and `read_docs` and `watch_video` have neither an `action` nor a `tracked_event` (r-checklist-single-activation-item); the Day 0 email has `cta_count` 2 and a `cta_url` that is the site root, the Day 3 email links to `/login` and is `send_condition: always` after Day 0 (r-email-one-cta-direct-link, r-email-sequence-suppressed-on-activation); the guide has `guides_on_screen` 3 and `hidden_after_step_complete` false (r-in-app-guide-at-dropoff-only); and no `defer_live_tactic` branch exists (r-one-tactic-per-step-at-a-time). Once those are fixed the cross-field checks add: `t1` targets "onboarding", which is not a measured drop-off, with a made-up 0.5 baseline (tactic-without-target-step); two items claim `activation_event: true` and the real one is not `required`; the Day 10 email is past the 7-day window; `t2` and `t3` both target "project created" with no shared `experiment_id` (two-tactics-same-step); the guide sits on `/dashboard`, not on the step's `/projects/new` (tooltip-stack); and `t2` and `t3` have no rollout step, so nothing states when they would be removed (r-exit-criterion-states-metric-and-threshold). What the reviewer sees: a feature tour disguised as a checklist and three tactics whose effect on one step cannot be told apart.
